doghouse.name: Doghouse ornaments (makes 6): 10" foam-board doghouses, red brick walls, cream shingle roof, arched door with cream trim, cream paw on the gable
doghouse.notes: Built at the board's scale: its doghouse is about as tall as the dog beside it (10-15"). Foam board keeps each one near 90 g, light enough for a sturdy branch.
doghouse.how: Print the template (pages 1-2, actual size, 11x17) and cut 6 sets from the foam board with a fresh blade: front with the arched door, back, two sides, two roof panels, floor, and the trim strips. Score brick lines on the walls and shingle rows on the roof with a ballpoint pen. Hot-glue the walls to the floor, thread a 30 cm gold loop through the ridge and glue on the roof (3/4" overhang). Paint the walls mortar grey (gesso + a drop of black), then sponge-dab barn red (Naphthol Red + Crimson 1:1) so the scored lines stay grey. Paint inside the door dark brown, the roof, corner trims and door arch cream, and stencil a 2.5" cream paw on the gable. About 25 min each once cut.

doghouse_small.name: Doghouse ornaments (makes 12): 4.3" foam-board doghouses

doghouse_xl.name: Giant doghouse (makes 1): 24 x 20 x 26" from two moving boxes, red brick walls, cream shingle roof, "Home for the Howlidays" sign
doghouse_xl.notes: Not on the board: an extra we can add for impact. The plush pair sits in the doorway.
doghouse_xl.how: Box A: cut all four walls down to 16", keep the bottom flaps taped as the floor. Cut the 10 x 13" arched door in a 24" side (template pages 6-7). Box B: cut two 24 x 10" gable triangles from its long flaps and glue them on top of the front and back walls; cut two 17.6 x 24" roof panels from its 24 x 20" sides. Score brick lines on all walls with a ballpoint pen. Gesso the outside twice (tinted grey), dab red bricks with a sponge, paint the inside dark red-brown. Glue the roof on, then cover it with 3" strips cut from the remaining flaps, overlapping 1" per course, and paint them cream. Glue on a cream trim strip round the door, stencil a 3.6" cream paw on the gable, and Mod Podge the printed 16 x 4" sign under the roof edge. About 4 hours over two sessions.

faux_treats.name: Faux dog biscuits (makes 60): foam clay cut with the bone cutters, painted biscuit-tan, sealed; fill the jar round a kraft-paper core

faux_treats.how: Roll clay 1/4" thick, cut 60 bones with the 3" cutter, poke dots with a toothpick, dry, paint tan (gesso + burnt sienna) and seal. Stand a crumpled kraft-paper log in the jar and fill the gap between it and the glass with biscuits, flat against the glass; pile the rest on top.

topper_4in.name: Tree topper (makes 1): 24" four-loop bow from 4" wired burlap with black felt paws
topper_4in.notes: The earlier design: four loops of 4" ribbon. Thinner and busier than the board's two fat loops.
topper_4in.how: Cut 2.6 yd of the 4" burlap. Glue on 20 black felt paws (2.2" template, page 3). Make four 6" loops (two up, two down), pinch with floral wire, wrap the centre, leave two 16" tails.

topper_printed.name: Tree topper (makes 1): 20" bow from ready-printed 2.5" burlap paw ribbon (brown paws)
topper_printed.notes: No cutting or gluing, but the paws are brown and the ribbon is less than half the board's width.
topper_printed.how: Make a four-loop bow, 20" across, with two 14" tails; pinch with floral wire and zip-tie to the top.

velvet_ribbon.name: Dark red wired velvet ribbon, 1.5" x 25 yd (bows on the paw ornaments and the jar)
velvet_ribbon.form_name: Dark red velvet ribbon, 1.5" x 25 yd
velvet_ribbon.notes: The board's paw-ornament and jar bows are deep red wired velvet with soft loops and long tails. MEEDEE "dark red" is that colour; hand-tied, a 9" bow uses about 1 yd.
